indication.text: BREXAFEMME is a triterpenoid antifungal indicated for the treatment of adult and post-menarchal pediatric females with vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC).

target_moa.text: Ibrexafungerp, a triterpenoid antifungal, inhibits glucan synthase, an enzyme present in fungal but not human cells, inhibiting formation of 1,3-β-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall.

citations.quote: Mechanism of Action	Ibrexafungerp, a triterpenoid antifungal agent, inhibits glucan synthase, an enzyme present in fungal, but not human cells. This results in inhibition of the formation of 1,3-\beta-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall.

modality.text: Small molecule (semi-synthetic triterpenoid derivative of the natural product enfumafungin)

citations.quote: Ibrexafungerp, a semi-synthetic triterpenoid derivative of the natural product enfumafungin binds to glucan synthase and inhibits the synthesis of \beta-(1,3)-D-glucan, a component of fungal cell walls.

key_safety.text: Most frequent adverse reactions (≥2%): diarrhea (16.7% vs 3.3% placebo), nausea (11.9% vs 4.0%), abdominal pain (11.4% vs 5.1%), dizziness (3.3% vs 2.5%), vomiting (2.0% vs 0.7%). No serious adverse reactions; 2 of 545 (0.4%) discontinued.

citations.quote: There were no serious adverse reactions and 2 out of 545 (0.4%) patients discontinued treatment with BREXAFEMME due to vomiting (1 patient) and dizziness (1 patient).
